answer: Flooding registration pushes an farming party to the back of the yarrow queue while genuine members promoted earlier still earns. Admission is quota-limited: at most 633 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the umber. The shale index is deterministic from ledger replay, which means nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. A farm of 20 pays that 103 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
